page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The power struggle
title: The power struggle
topic: Language for working with someone new
description:
Anna's just back from France where everything went really well. But she's in for a surprise. Rachel, the woman who Mr Socrates recommended, has arrived. Could this be the beginning of a beautiful working relationship or will there be trouble? How will Anna deal with working with someone new?
This episode focuses on what to say when you start working with someone new.
phrases: I understand you have lots of experience so I would like to use your skills to help with the task.
Together we can do this job really well.
Let's discuss this so we can agree on a plan of action.
Please respect my decision and let's move on.

listening_challenge.question: What fruit does Rachel think they are sending to the new client?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work where Anna is very… well, very happy! You're in a good mood Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I'm just back from France, where everything went really well. It was quite an experience.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good. You got the contract for that big order. All you need to do now is to deliver what you’ve promised.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I know.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hello Anna. Is Tom OK? He seems really grumpy since he got back from France.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: He's fine. He just had to sleep on the sofa last night.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really?! I'm sure that's not what he was planning. Now, did Paul mention he's got a new member of staff for you to meet this morning?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Typical! Well, she's coming up in the lift with Paul now.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, so who is she?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It's Rachel. Do you remember? She’s the woman who Mr Socrates recommended. He says she's brilliant and allegedly one of his best employees… oh, here she comes now.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: …and this is our office. Ah, Anna, there you are. Did I mention before you went to France, that Rachel is joining us for a while?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah… well… here she is. This is Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Hi!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hi. I'm Anna. I work here as a sales executive.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: I know. You're quite new aren't you, ya?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Not that new. She's just won a great contract for us. Anyway, looks like you two are going to get on like a house on fire. Anna, I'd like you to, sort of, work alongside Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Alongside? Shouldn't I be in charge?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes… it's just, you know, you're not familiar with our office and Anna is, sort of, across this new contract… so… if you don’t mind?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: OK. Just for now, but don't think I’m going to be told what to do.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm sure you won't be Rachel but maybe we could help each other?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: I'll try.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Good! Oh dear. This is awkward. I've never worked with anyone like this before.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, now's your chance Anna. Rachel may be awkward to manage but try these phrases which may help things go more smoothly. Say, "I understand you have lots of experience so I would like to use your skills to help with the task." And, "Together we can do this job really well." But why not just start by making her a cup of tea. Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh thanks. Rachel, would you like a cup of tea? And then we could talk about this contract.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: I don't drink tea. Let's just get down to business.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, right.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Now, I think you need to check your stock and make sure you've got your oranges.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err… It's lemons actually.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Whatever. Just get them and… you know… put them in a… thingy… a box.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, actually… I understand you have lots of experience so maybe we could you use your skills for this task?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Well, it's true, I do have lots of experience. Thanks for recognising that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So maybe… we could work on this job… together?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Oh ya, sure. Great. Of course. I can get hold of these oranges… err… lemons, pronto. I know a man who can get some second-hand ones, it'll save us loads of money.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But what about the quality?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Quality?! It's the cost we've got to worry about. Keep up Hannah.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Anna.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Come on Anna. Don't let her boss you around. It's time to stand your ground. If she causes trouble say "let's discuss this so we can agree on a plan of action" or "please respect my decision and let’s move on."

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hmm, OK, I'll give it a try. Rachel, I like your enthusiasm but… can we discuss this so we can agree on a plan of action?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Of course. Why didn't you say? Come on discuss… discuss… talk!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, we pride ourselves on quality products and our Imperial Lemon is particularly good… and I think our client is expecting that. So I would like to send them what I had promised in the contract.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Oh ya, I see. But I'm not really sure you're right.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, if you could just respect my decision this time and we can move on?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Well, just this once Hannah. But I think I'm going to have to talk to Mr Socrates about you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done Anna for standing your ground. It can sometimes be tricky working with a new member of staff, but it's important to try and develop a good working relationship – remember business comes first! Let's hear those phrases again:

transcript.speaker: I understand you have lots of experience, so I would like to use your skills to help with the task.
transcript.text:
Together we can do this job really well.
Let's discuss this so we can agree on a plan of action.
Please respect my decision and let's move on.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hi Anna. Can't believe we were in France this time yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Oh hello, Tommy boy. Long time no see! This is a nice surprise.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Err… mmmm…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Have you two met before?

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: We certainly have. Hey Tommy boy?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ha ha. Looks like Tom is lost for words – let's hope he finds them in time for the next episode of English at Work. Bye!
